goal: Keep BASIC short while preserving information needed for safety and evidence-linked rules.
design_decisions: The master question bank remains broad; the UI does not ask every question.
BASIC has a small universal core.
Many dietary/lifestyle/symptom items become rule-specific and are asked only if needed.
Medication and current supplement use remain early safety screens.
Specific safety conditions can be presented as one compact multi-item screen even though stored as separate structured variables.
PRO contains detailed diet, laboratory, anthropometric, and history questions.
Future Phase 2 rules may promote a rule-specific question into the universal core if evidence shows it is broadly necessary.

estimated_basic_experience.note: Pregnancy/lactation and safety fields should be hidden when not applicable; conditional follow-ups appear only when triggered.
estimated_basic_experience.target_ui_screens: Approximately 10–14 compact screens/cards, depending on branching; not 44 sequential questions.

removal_or_demotions.reason: Nonspecific symptom; should not be a universal driver of supplement recommendation.
Nonspecific; ask only when relevant to a validated rule or user goal.
Broad symptom category; better used as a branch trigger.
Useful for selected administration/sleep/performance contexts, not every supplement.
Retain in bank; activate for rules where alcohol materially changes relevance or safety.
Important for calcium-related rules but unnecessary for every user if those rules are not under evaluation.
